title: Structured acceptance ritual and remote setup guide
content:
Purpose:
This is a practical, lightweight playbook for candidate acceptance and the remote first-week setup. The goal: convert verbal/offer acceptances into a calm, predictable first 7 days so engineers and managers can focus on momentum, not logistics.

TL;DR (2-line summary):
- Run an "acceptance ritual" (quick human-touch steps) within 24 hours of verbal yes.
- Kick-off provisioning and calendar choreography immediately (IT, manager, buddy). Confirm everything is green 48–72 hours before start.

Why this exists (context):
We frequently see delays after offer-accept. Typical causes: equipment lag, unclear manager expectations, missed orientation invites, cloud account/permissions friction. For remote hires the human signal at offer-to-accept is hugely important for retention. This doc codifies a repeatable, low-effort ritual and an operational checklist so people-ops, manager, and SRE/IT have clear handoffs.

Acceptance ritual (first 24 hours) — owner: recruiter + people-ops
- Recruiter: phone call to candidate (10 minutes) to celebrate, outline the first week vibe, confirm start date and timezone, and ask about personal device preferences. Script bullets: 
  - "Congrats — we’re thrilled. Two immediate things: a short manager welcome call this week, and our IT will start provisioning. Any constraints we should know?"
  - Ask about commute/equipment preferences, ADA accommodations, and home internet quirks.
- People-ops: send the "Welcome & Next Steps" email template (copy below) within 2 hours.
- People-ops: create a temporary onboarding ticket in JIRA (JIRA-HIRE-987 style) with due dates for equipment, access, and training invites.

Welcome & Next Steps (email template) — send this ASAP
Subject: Welcome to Redwood — quick next steps before Day 1
Hi <Name>,
Welcome again — excited you’re joining the team on <Start Date>! A few quick items we’ll take care of:
- We’ll provision your laptop and send a tracking link.
- You’ll get calendar invites for Day 0 (setup), Day 1 orientation, and a buddy meet-and-greet.
- Please reply if you need any adjustments to start time or accommodations.
One-pager attached: Day 0 checklist and manager contact.
Jordan (on behalf of People Ops)

Manager checklist — owner: hiring manager (complete no later than 7 days before start)
- Book a 30-min intro call during the offer/accept week (informal: expectations, team culture, first-week goals).
- Create Day 1 1:1 + team intro calendar events and add new hire; invite buddy.
- Draft 30/60/90 goals (high level; one paragraph) and share in the intro call.
- Ensure codebase access request is submitted (include repo names), and list any onboarding PRs the new hire should start with.
- Identify 1st-week project with minimal setup (reading + small commit).

IT / Provisioning checklist — owner: infra/sourcing coordinator
- Confirm whether hire is company laptop or BYOD; if company laptop, order and expedite shipping.
- Create cloud accounts and add to base infra groups (staging, slack, vignette).
- Provision required permissions for 1st-week tasks (read access to internal docs, repo read, sandbox environment).
- Ship a "remote staging kit" (laptop + power adapters + basic dock or recommended home peripherals list). Include quick-start Wi-Fi tips and support hours.
- Track asset shipping with a public tracking string in the onboarding JIRA ticket.

Day 0 (remote setup day) — recommended cadence
- 10:00 local: Day 0 "setup" (30–60m) with People Ops to walk through accounts and benefits paperwork; confirm KMS and MFA enrollment.
- 11:00 local: IT 1:1 to confirm laptop receipt and run baseline diagnostics.
- Afternoon: self-directed tasks: Slack join, read team README, quick tour of docs.
- End of day: manager check-in (15 min) — welcome + confirm Day 1 schedule.

Day 1 (orientation) — manager + people-ops
- Company orientation (60–90m): culture, security basics, benefits overview.
- Team introduction (30m): team goals, current sprint, quick wins.
- Buddy pairing (15m): lightweight expectations, standup cadence.

Day 2–5 — momentum week
- 1:1 with manager to set immediate learning plan (30m)
- 1–2 small onboarding tasks (read + comment PR, fix a documentation bug)
- Schedule a role-specific deep-dive with teammate (60m)
- End-of-week: 30-min retro with manager + buddy on blockers and next steps

Quick interview debrief / scorecard (for hiring manager + debriefers) — this is intentionally minimal so we can file quick hires without slow debate
- Criteria (score 1–5 each): Technical fit, Problem solving, Communication, Teamwork, Role enthusiasm.
- Pass threshold: average >= 3.5 and no 1s in critical dimensions.
- Note: if candidate requires upskilling in one area but is an otherwise strong cultural fit, attach a 30-day success plan to the offer.

30/60/90 sample template (one paragraph each)
- 30: Get repo and local dev env running, ship a documentation or test improvement.
- 60: Complete two small feature tickets with owner-level reviews and participate in cross-team sync.
- 90: Own a small feature area and lead a retro on an onboarding improvement.

Buddy handshake (micro-ritual to improve retention)
- Buddy sends a public Slack welcome message on Day 0 and schedules a 15-min coffee chat Day 1.
- Buddy helps with the first code PR and gives the new hire a "first PR" badge in Slack.

Escalation and edge-cases
- If equipment shipping exceeds 5 business days, offer a temporary stipend for hardware or arrange a loaner.
- For international hires: confirm customs and local tax forms 3 weeks out.

Open questions / unresolved items (notes-to-self)
- Should we standardize the "first PR" badge copy/design with DEX? (Priya to own mock)
- Can we pre-bundle a zero-config dev container for common stacks? (Evan to prototype)
- Confirm legal sign-off on expedited shipping costs for contractors vs full-time.

Related artifacts & checklist links
- JIRA template: JIRA-HIRE-987
- Confluence draft for Day 0 scripts: confluence://people-ops/onboard-staging-2025
- Slack channel for announcements: #people-ops (use thread "welcome-rituals")

Retrospective prompt (complete at 4 weeks)
- What from the acceptance ritual made the candidate feel supported?
- What operational friction delayed Day 1?
- What automation saved time?

Notes to reviewers:
- This is intentionally lean and people-first — please flag any legal or procurement constraints that require additional lead time.
- Looking for volunteers to trial the "remote staging kit" and the first-PR badge for hires in Q4 2025.

Footer: Jordan Lee, People Ops — draft v0.3
